commits.message:
A split host settles a stalled escape sequence after the escape delay (rich-host-input-gnl7)

On a "split" host only a lone ESC was held on a timer; an `ESC [` or
`ESC O` left at a read's end waited forever and took the next key as
its final byte. Any unfinished escape sequence is now held for
ESCAPE_DELAY_MS (100, Textual's ESCAPE_DELAY and vim's ttimeoutlen) and
then settled by the whole-keys rule: `ESC [` alone is Alt+[, any other
ESC is Escape with the rest read again.

The delay replaces the 0ms lone-ESC timer, so a lone ESC split from its
`[A` over ssh now completes too. Costs: Escape on a real tty is heard
after 100ms, and Escape then `[` typed within 100ms reads as Alt+[.

A whole-keys host settles each input chunk (rich-host-input-ab9n) (#393)

* A whole-keys host settles each input chunk; no lone ESC is held for a timer (rich-host-input-ab9n)

TerminalHost declares inputChunks: xterm.js (BrowserTerminalHost, and the
docs worker's simulated stdin through NodeTerminalHost) never splits a key
across chunks, so an ESC left at a chunk's end is Escape and what followed
it is re-read. A tty stays "split" and keeps the setTimeout(0) hold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Whole-keys settle: ESC [ / ESC O is the Alt chord; settling survives a throwing sink (rich-host-input-ab9n)

Review fixes: whole-keys feed no longer runs the split hold logic; header
names InputChunks; docs Input field typed; integration test that a
NodeTerminalHost in the docs worker reads whole-keys. Split-host residue
filed as rich-host-input-gnl7.

* Whole-keys settle reads a chunk's rest in full when a sink throws mid-drain (rich-host-input-ab9n)
